LanguageData.SR.About.Name: Squeaky Ratkin
LanguageData.SR.About.Description:
Squeaky Ratkin is a lightweight sound effect mod that injects a little stir into the Ratkin experience. It brings a whimsical medley of chirps and squeaks to these once-silent little critters, ensuring every action comes with... a little sound things. No longer shall the colonies and the world beyond echo solely with the lamentations of blood and fire - the whispered squeaks of the ratkin will remind you that though they may be small, they are never content to remain silent.
*Not eligible for registration in The Book of Squeakudges*

LanguageData.SR.DevTools.AudioBrowser.Short: Inspect loaded animal voice material in a separate window.

Material previews require explicit Resolve and test a selected loaded clip; final Ratkin preview uses a selected pawn and the current production path. Opening it does not enable statistics, detailed logging, or successful dispatch recording.

LanguageData.SR.DevTools.Logging.Short: Choose whether supported human-readable log events include additional stable diagnostic fields.

It is independent of RimWorld Dev Mode, action statistics, successful dispatch recording, and the seven-click tool unlock. More detail helps troubleshooting but increases log volume.

LanguageData.SR.DevTools.Logging.Mode.Tooltip.Enabled: Always include detailed srdiag fields for supported log events. This can increase log volume but does not enable RimWorld Dev Mode or the other diagnostic tools.
LanguageData.SR.DevTools.Logging.Mode.Tooltip.Disable: Suppress detailed srdiag fields even when the build default would enable them. Normal human-readable warnings and errors remain available.

LanguageData.SR.Global.PageDesc: All behavior, timing, distance, Mood, and voice settings apply immediately. Changes are saved automatically.
LanguageData.SR.Rules.PageDesc: Control how often Ratkin squeak, how far they can be heard, and which actions may produce a sound. Changes take effect immediately and save automatically.
LanguageData.SR.ActionEnable.Short: Choose when each squeak action is allowed to run.
LanguageData.SR.ActionEnable.Tooltip: Changes apply immediately and save automatically. Disabled actions stop before random checks, cooldowns, voice checks, sound selection, playback, and action timestamps. Draft and Undraft share a visual group but remain separate settings.
LanguageData.SR.ActionScope.Tooltip: Choose the trigger scope for {0}. “Any eligible” includes automatic and player-driven occurrences; “player command” accepts only the supported player-issued path. Disabled prevents the action from entering its normal trigger pipeline.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Short: Voice packs change sound source only; frequency, eligibility, distance, and Mood rules remain unchanged.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.NoBiotechShort: Biotech is unavailable. Xenotype sources are dormant; the current policy uses only sources that remain available.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.Off: Off uses the built-in Vanilla fallback only. It does not mute Ratkin.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.Fallback: Fallback tries the pawn's exact Xenotype layer, then the shared Ratkin Race layer, then Vanilla.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.Remix: Remix chooses equally among currently playable Xenotype, Race, and Vanilla layers; eligible packs within a pack layer also participate equally.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.NoBiotech.Off: Without Biotech, Off still uses Vanilla only. It does not mute Ratkin, and Race packs do not participate in this mode.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.NoBiotech.Fallback: Without Biotech, the Xenotype layer is unavailable, so Fallback tries the shared Ratkin Race layer and then Vanilla.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.NoBiotech.Remix: Without Biotech, Remix chooses equally among the currently playable Race and Vanilla layers. Eligible Race packs also participate equally within the Race layer.
LanguageData.SR.VoiceSource.Help.Common: Voice packs change sound source only, never frequency, eligibility, listening distance, or Mood.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.PageDesc: Choose a voice-source policy, then assign installed packs below. Changes apply and save immediately.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Mode.Desc.Fallback: Fallback in order: Xenotype, Race, then Vanilla.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Mode.Desc.Remix: Mix all playable source layers equally.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Mode.Tooltip.Off: Only the built-in Vanilla fallback participates in playback. Pack assignments remain saved and editable, ready for another mode. Voice packs never change action frequency, cooldowns, eligibility, or Mood settings.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Mode.Tooltip.Fallback: For each action, try the pawn's exact Xenotype assignment first, then the Ratkin Race assignment, then the built-in Vanilla fallback. A missing action in one layer falls through to the next. Voice packs change sound source only, never behavior or frequency.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Mode.Tooltip.Remix: For each action, choose equally among the currently playable Xenotype, Race, and Vanilla layers. Within a pack layer, eligible packs are also chosen equally before their sounds. Missing layers are skipped. Voice packs change sound source only.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.InstalledSummary: Ready to assign: {0} Race pack(s), {1} Xenotype pack(s).
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Installed.Tooltip: This list includes voice packs that passed validation. Names and authors are attribution only; they do not change selection weight. A pack supplies sounds for covered actions and cannot change action frequency, cooldowns, eligibility, distance, or Mood rules.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.RemixConfirm.Title: Enable equal-weight Remix?
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.RemixConfirm1.Body: Remix can make the voice source change from one action to the next. It gives each currently playable Xenotype, Race, and Vanilla tier equal weight; it does not prioritize a preferred pack.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.RemixConfirm2.Body: Confirm equal-weight mixing. Playback may alternate noticeably between installed packs and Vanilla. This changes only the source policy; your selections remain saved.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Domain.Tooltip: Assignments apply immediately and save automatically. Multiple eligible packs in this same layer have equal weight; each chosen pack then selects from its own sounds. Coverage can differ by action, so normal fallback still applies.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.Domain.Tooltip.Short: Assignments apply immediately. Multiple selected packs in this source layer participate equally.
LanguageData.SR.VoicePack.OffNotice: OFF is active: selections are retained and editable, but packs do not participate in playback.

Existing choices and presets are retained, but new packs cannot be enabled for this layer.

LanguageData.SR.Xeno.ConflictSelectionRetained: Existing selections are retained. You may disable packs individually or forget the full selection.

Existing saved keys remain available for recovery; forgetting them does not resolve the definition conflict.
LanguageData.SR.Xeno.RaceDefaultLayer.Tooltip: The Race layer applies to Ratkin regardless of Xenotype. Fallback tries an exact Xenotype assignment before this shared layer; without Biotech, playback can still use Race and then Vanilla.
LanguageData.SR.Xeno.RaceDefaultLayer.InlineHelp: The shared Race layer applies to Ratkin regardless of Xenotype. Fallback tries an exact Xenotype assignment first, then this layer, then Vanilla. Without Biotech, Race and Vanilla remain available.
LanguageData.SR.Xeno.Availability.Tooltip: Dormant or unloaded targets keep their saved settings. A conflicting exact defName disables only that Xenotype layer and its new assignments; global behavior and Race/Vanilla fallback continue.
LanguageData.SR.Xeno.BehaviorSummary.Tooltip: Every field marked Inherit follows its current Global value. Enabling an override changes only that exact Xenotype and applies immediately. The exact defName, not the localized label, identifies the target.
LanguageData.SR.Xeno.BehaviorSummary.Tooltip.Short: Inherited fields follow the current global value. Overrides affect only this exact Xenotype and apply immediately.

LanguageData.SR.Xeno.NoTargets: No Xenotype targets are currently declared, saved, or discovered.

LanguageData.SR.Xeno.RaceSummary.Tooltip.Short: The shared Ratkin Race layer remains available without Biotech and changes sound source only.

LanguageData.SR.AudioPoolNotice.Title: Voice packs available
LanguageData.SR.AudioPoolNotice.Body: Voice packs were found but none are selected for the following targets. Playback still follows the current voice-pack mode:
LanguageData.SR.ScaleCooldownWithTimeSpeed.Label: Keep squeak pacing steady at higher game speeds
LanguageData.SR.ScaleCooldownWithTimeSpeed.Tooltip: When enabled, trigger cooldowns grow with the current game speed so fast-forward does not create a burst of squeaks in real time. This scales cooldown duration, not playback volume or action probability.
LanguageData.SR.ScaleFrequencyWithTalking.Label: Scale ordinary squeak attempts with Talking capacity
LanguageData.SR.ScaleFrequencyWithTalking.Short: Lower Talking makes ordinary squeak attempts less likely.
LanguageData.SR.ScaleFrequencyWithTalking.Tooltip: Ordinary attempts roll against the pawn's Talking capacity. A rejected roll still consumes that action's attempt cooldown and the shared cooldown when applicable. Death skips this Talking roll, but unusable vocal organs or pathways silence every action, including Death.
LanguageData.SR.ScalePeriodicWithAudiblePopulation.La: Reduce periodic squeaks in crowded audible areas
LanguageData.SR.ScalePeriodicWithAudiblePopulation.To: When more than 10 Ratkin are audible, periodic attempts slow down and random periodic chances are reduced progressively. Immediate feedback such as selection, drafting, wounds, combat, and death is unchanged.
LanguageData.SR.LocalizeDebugActions.Label: Translate this mod's debug-action names
LanguageData.SR.LocalizeDebugActions.Tooltip: Uses this mod's English or Simplified Chinese labels in RimWorld's developer action menu. Reopen that menu after changing the setting. This does not enable RimWorld Dev Mode or any diagnostic tool.
LanguageData.SR.GlobalCooldownMultiplier.Label: Master squeak interval: {0}x
LanguageData.SR.GlobalCooldownMultiplier.Tooltip: Scales both each action's own interval and the shared interval between attempts. Actions whose XML sets ignoreGlobalCooldown still ignore the shared interval, but their own interval is still scaled. At 0x these cooldown gates are removed; action probability, scope, eligibility, and Talking still apply.
LanguageData.SR.Distance.Preset.Tooltip: Presets copy their XML-defined start and end heights into the live range. Manual edits switch the label to Custom. Changes apply immediately and use RimWorld's camera-height scale, not map-cell distance from the pawn.
LanguageData.SR.Distance.Short: Full below {0}; fades to silence at {1}.
LanguageData.SR.Distance.Tooltip: This uses RimWorld's camera-height scale from 15 to 65. In-map sounds stay at full volume below the start, fade linearly through the range, and are silent above the end. The current-final-sound preview uses the real in-map path; material clip preview is on-camera and is not distance-attenuated.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.PageDesc: Adjust the pitch, volume, and variation applied to the chosen sound for each Mood. This does not change action frequency, eligibility, or voice-source selection.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.Scope.Short: Choose a Mood, then adjust its shared pitch and volume.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.Scope.Tooltip: These values are the Global layer used by every Ratkin unless an exact Xenotype field overrides them. They modify the chosen sound at playback and do not change voice-pack policy, action frequency, cooldowns, or eligibility. Changes apply immediately and save automatically.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.SearchAction: Search localized action name or action ID
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.EnableFirst: Enable custom values before editing them.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.InheritedReadOnly: This Mood inherits its XML defaults. Enable custom values to edit these parameters.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.Action.Tooltip: Selects which action supplies the material SoundDef and which action the final preview asks the selected Ratkin to play. This selector does not change production action settings.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.Override.Tooltip: Enabled uses the custom values shown below for this Mood. Disabled inherits the XML defaults. The switch and values apply immediately; Xenotype fields can still override individual values later.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.Preset.Tooltip: Loads a complete pitch, volume, and jitter combination, enables the custom Mood override, and applies it immediately. Presets do not change voice source or action behavior.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.MaterialPreview.Short: Material preview tests one resolved clip only.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.MaterialPreview.Tooltip: Resolve explicitly loads the selected action's material clips, then Preview sends one chosen clip through the on-camera sample adapter with the current Mood values. It does not use the production resolver, pawn, voice-pack tier, distance path, probability, or cooldown. A dispatched result does not prove that a silent placeholder is audible.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.MaterialPreview.Tooltip.Sho: Tests one resolved material clip with the current Mood values. It does not use the final pawn or voice-source path.
LanguageData.SR.SoundMood.PreviewNote: Previews are explicit test requests. A dispatched request does not confirm audible output.
LanguageData.SR.MaterialPreview.Resolve.NoClips: Resolve completed, but no material clips are available. {1}
LanguageData.SR.MaterialPreview.Reason.NoClips: No resolved material clips are available.
LanguageData.SR.MaterialPreview.Reason.AdapterMissing: The material preview camera adapter is unavailable.
LanguageData.SR.MaterialPreview.Reason.SampleFailed: The resolved material clip could not be sampled.
LanguageData.SR.MaterialPreview.Reason.Dispatched: Material clip preview dispatched. Audible output is not confirmed.
LanguageData.SR.Settings.Save.Tooltip: Settings take effect immediately. Disk writes are grouped briefly to avoid writing once per slider step. “Saving…” means a write is queued; “Saved” confirms the latest queued values were written. “Save failed” means the current session changed but those values may not survive a restart.
LanguageData.SR.FinalPreview.Short: Hear the path currently chosen for the selected Ratkin.
LanguageData.SR.FinalPreview.Tooltip: Uses the selected spawned Ratkin, current voice mode, exact Xenotype and Race assignments, fallback, current Mood, and the real in-map sound path. It bypasses probability and cooldown gates, does not add action statistics, and does not claim audible success. Silent placeholders can still return Dispatched.
LanguageData.SR.FinalPreview.Tooltip.Short: Uses the selected Ratkin and current production source, Mood, and in-map path while bypassing probability and cooldown.
LanguageData.SR.FinalPreview.NoPawn: Select a spawned Ratkin on the current map.

LanguageData.SR.Stats.StartFailed: Select a spawned Ratkin on the current map.
LanguageData.SR.Stats.Random: startup wait {0} · checks {1} · pass {2} · expected {3} · observed {4} · sent {5}
LanguageData.SR.Stats.Funnel: enter {0} → scope/off {1} → startup wait {2} → cooldown {3} → vocal {4} → audio {5} → sent {6}
LanguageData.SR.Stats.Short: Records one selected Ratkin until stopped or invalid.
LanguageData.SR.Stats.Tooltip: Statistics are memory-only and never saved. Start Selected clears the previous counters and records only that spawned Ratkin. Preview Final does not count. Counts begin at try_trigger_enter; work rejected before TryTrigger by map, view, or unconfigured-action checks is outside this report. This tool does not enable detailed logging, successful dispatch recording, or the audio browser.
LanguageData.SR.Stats.Columns.Tooltip: The denominator is try_trigger_enter: an attempt counts only after entering TryTrigger. Rejections before that point—map, view, or an unconfigured action—are excluded. Random one-shot actions show probability checks, passes, average expected probability, observed pass rate, and dispatches. Each-time and external actions show the funnel through scope or disabled state, cooldowns, vocal-capability checks, audio failures, and dispatch.
LanguageData.SR.AudioPath.Short: Keep the 10 most recent successful dispatches in memory.
LanguageData.SR.AudioPath.Enabled.Tooltip: Records successful production dispatches, including action, source tier, SoundDef, and voice-pack attribution. When enabled, production dispatches briefly show their result. Recording does not enable RimWorld Dev Mode, action statistics, detailed logging, or the audio browser.
LanguageData.SR.AudioPath.RecordHint: Click ? to show source details and clip limits below.
